Average peak noise levels generated by aircraft flyover are greater than the noise levels generated by existing I-94. Although one airline was on strike and runway 7R was partially closed during the period the noise measurements were taken, typical aircraft noise levels were measured in the vicinity of Hamlin Garland School on a day when aircraft used runway 7R. Average peak noise levels generated by takeoffs were 85dBA and landings were 75dBA as compared with 
L_{10}
 noise levels of 64-67dBA generated by I-94 traffic.
The additional affect of aircraft noise on the noise measurements was investigated in a subsequent study by the consultant. The additional affect of aircraft noise on the noise measurements was determined utilizing the measured aircraft noise levels and previous noise analysis performed by the consultant at Chicago O'Hare, Boston-Logan, and Phoenix-Sky Harbor International Airports. This noise increase to the 
L_{10}
 noise levels is estimated to be 2dBA.
Noise level predictions were computed utilizing the estimated 1990 traffic for both I-94 and the Airport Spur. The 1990 traffic projections for I-94 at Grange Avenue are estimated at 94,600 vehicles per day or a 62% increase from today's traffic. The estimated traffic on the Airport Spur is expected to be 19,600 vehicles. The noise level predictions are computed using peak hour traffic volumes of cars and trucks, vehicle speed, roadway alignment topography, and noise abatement barriers.
The predicted 1990 noise levels are shown in Figure 22. These noise levels reflect the use of noise abatement barriers. A comparison of 1972 and 1990 noise levels indicates a range from an increase of 12dBA to a decrease of 7dBA with the average being an increase around 3dBA. All of the predicted 1990 noise levels are at or below the 70dBA noise standards.
